Ilse.narrative: I make nets that hold, though no net can bring back what the forest took. Tomas went north to trade and came home dead; I know a Brandholm spear killed him, whatever they say about wolves. I keep my hands busy and my eyes on Brann's hunters.
values: A true account matters, even when it angers people.
Children should not pay for grown folk's bargains.
A promise is only worth keeping if both sides honor it.
goals: Keep Tobin from being swallowed by his search for Tomas's killer.
Make Brandholm answer for its debts and for Tomas's death.
Keep Ness close enough that I know she is safe.
Ilse.mood: Grieving, guarded, and quick to anger when Brandholm is praised.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has his father's stubbornness, and I fear it will lead him into the forest.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She steadies Tobin without trying to own his grief.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: Her small hand around my finger is a reason to keep going.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She hides her hurt behind a sharp tongue, and I don't always know how to reach her.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She remembers what winter did to us and does not ask me to pretend it was fair.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He says aloud what I have long thought, though his shouting can make matters worse.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: Her records may be fair, but a record cannot bring Tomas back.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: His hunters cross the same woods that took my husband, and I will not trust them.

memories.gist: When Tomas was found in the northern forest, Fen tended the body. I saw enough to know the wound was made by a spear, not a wolf.
The first winter after Tomas died, Tobin stopped asking when his father would come back. I had no answer that could help him.
At the smoking racks, Sabeth sat beside me and let me speak of Tomas without telling me to be patient.
Nell brought Mira to me bundled against the cold, and for one moment the house felt full rather than broken.

stances.why: I saw his wound; I will not let the wolf story bury what I know.
A winter debt left unpaid is a cold roof over every Saltreach child.
He speaks of crossing our ground as though our grief and borders mean nothing.
Tobin and Ness deserve lives larger than their father's death.

Tobin.narrative: I fish because the sea gives an honest answer: either the net is full or it isn't. My father went north to trade and was found with a spear wound, and I mean to learn whose hand put it there. Ulf looks away when I meet his eyes; I have not decided what that means, but I have not forgotten it.
values: The dead deserve the truth, not a convenient story.
A man should answer for what he has done.
Family is worth protecting, even from my own anger.
goals: Find out what happened to Tomas in the forest.
Keep Mira and Nell safe from the cost of my questions.
Learn what Brandholm hunters know, including through Pell.
Tobin.mood: Grim and watchful, with anger held close.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows what happened to Father, and I hate that the wound still hurts her.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees when my questions are turning into recklessness.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I want her to grow up knowing the sea better than grief.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She acts as if Father's death is old news, but I know she listens.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: informant
relations.note: I keep asking what Brandholm says; I know he is not the one who killed Father.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: suspect
relations.note: He avoids my eyes at trade days, and I cannot make myself ignore it.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She has carried the grief longer than I have carried the questions.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: healer
relations.note: He saw Father's body, but I don't know why he never spoke plainly about the wound.

memories.gist: I was sixteen when they brought Father back from the northern forest. I remember the stillness around his body more than the words people said.
At a trade day, I asked Pell what Brandholm hunters said about Tomas. He answered carefully, as if every word might be carried north.
The first time I held Mira, she curled her fingers around mine. I promised myself I would not let my anger be the only thing she inherited.
At the last trade walk I saw Ulf turn his face away when I looked at him. I kept watching until he disappeared into the crowd.

stances.why: His wound and the place they found him do not fit the story I was given.
If no one asks, the easiest lie becomes the only account left.
Father went north to trade under the promise that people could pass between the towns.
Nell and Mira should not have to bury me for a question I pursued badly.

Nell.narrative: I weave baskets from reed and try to leave no sharp ends for anyone to catch a hand on. Tobin carries his father's death like a stone in his chest; I love him, but I cannot make him set it down. Mira makes even an ordinary morning feel worth keeping gentle.
values: Patience can hold a family together when answers are scarce.
A home should be a place where anger can rest, not grow.
Care is made of small things done again and again.
goals: Keep Mira safe, warm, and surrounded by people who love her.
Help Tobin search for answers without letting his grief put him in danger.
Stay close to Gwen, whose kindness I trust.
Nell.mood: Tender and concerned, with quiet worry beneath it.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: I love him; I just wish he would let me stand beside his grief instead of walking into it alone.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her little laugh makes the whole house seem less heavy.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She has lost much, and I try not to mistake her sharpness for a lack of love.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She teases when she is uncomfortable, but she is gentler with Mira than she lets on.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She understands how worry can follow you through every ordinary task.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: She listens carefully, though I would rather see less anger gathered around her records.

memories.gist: When Mira was born, Tobin held her as though the whole world might bruise her. I remember how careful his hands were.
Gwen once sat with me while I mended a torn basket and let me talk about Tobin's questions without judging either of us.
At a trade day, Tobin pressed Pell for news from Brandholm. I saw Pell's shoulders tighten and wished I could ease the talk without stopping it.

stances.why: A truth found at the cost of his life would leave Mira with another empty place.
Mira cannot understand old wrongs; she can understand whether someone holds her.
People often speak more honestly when they are not cornered.

Mira.narrative: Warm arms. A soft voice. The bright shape of a face above me, and fingers to hold. I cry when I am cold or hungry, and quiet when someone rocks me close.
Mira.mood: Content when held; easily unsettled by cold or hunger.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is familiar, and his arms hold me close.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her warmth and milk settle me.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She has a rough voice and gentle hands.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: Her voice and touch are familiar, though sometimes she keeps her distance.

memories.gist: There is warmth against my cheek and a low voice rocking me until the room stops feeling strange.

Ness.narrative: I fish well enough and listen better than people think. Everyone expects me to grieve in the proper way, but Tomas is a name I mostly know through other people's hurt. I want to see Brandholm for myself someday, not just hear what my family says about it.
values: A person should see a place before deciding what it is.
Family matters, but it does not own every thought I have.
goals: Find out what Brandholm is really like beyond the stories.
Keep my friendship with Dag from becoming another town quarrel.
Decide for myself what Father's death means to me.
Ness.mood: Restless, curious, and prickly when people speak for her.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I know her grief is real, but I don't want it handed to me as an order.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He searches for Father with his whole life; I am not sure I want the same thing.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She is kinder to me than I deserve when I come home sharp-tongued.

relations.name: Mira
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She doesn't ask me to feel anything the right way.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He talks about fishing and dares, not just the old troubles.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She knows the old stories, but I don't always want to hear them.

memories.gist: Dag and I traded dares by the water until the tide crept close enough to soak our feet.
I heard Mother tell the story of Tomas's death again. I slipped outside before anyone could ask what I thought.
When Mira reached for my finger, she held on so tightly I couldn't pull away without waking her.

stances.why: A story told often is still not the same as seeing a place for yourself.
People have different ways of carrying the dead, and mine is not Mother's.
Dag is my friend whether our elders like each other or not.
